transcript.text: Every so often when I use the hob the electrics in the house go off. Not every time, maybe once a week. It's an induction hob, Hisense I think.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. An induction hob tripping your electrics is almost always caused by an 'earth leak'—meaning electricity is escaping where it shouldn't, often from the internal power module or coil when they get hot. Because this involves mains wiring and high-voltage components, you must stop using the hob until a qualified engineer has checked it; repeatedly resetting the breaker to keep cooking is unsafe. To help them diagnose it safely once isolated: have there been any recent spillages near the control panel that might have seeped underneath? And does the trip happen on a specific heating zone, or is it random?

Yes, there have been a couple of boil-overs. I don't know which zone it is, it's usually when I've got two on high, and sometimes when something boils over. I also noticed a faint electrical smell once after it tripped.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Given the boil-overs near the controls, the electrical smell, and the fact that it trips when under load (two zones on high), this is probably an internal earth-leakage fault caused by moisture tracking into the live components. The combination of a burning smell and tripping electrics means there is likely damage to the insulation inside the power module or wiring. Please do not attempt to use the hob again, and do not try to reset the breaker to cook. You need to have it isolated at the consumer unit (switch off the dedicated circuit) and call a qualified electrician or appliance engineer to inspect and repair it safely.

candidates: Earth leakage in induction power module or coil (high)
Mains wiring or connection block fault (medium)
